article_content: In southern Spain, a vast network of greenhouses spans an area equivalent in size to the Isle of Wight. These structures supply a significant amount of fruit and vegetables to Britain and other European countries. The Almeria greenhouses have altered the local climate by reflecting sunlight, thus reducing the average temperature in the area. Workers in these greenhouses endure harsh conditions, laboring in high temperatures for low wages. The once barren landscape, previously used for filming 'spaghetti westerns', has been transformed using imported soil and advanced agricultural techniques. The workforce is predominantly composed of immigrants from Africa and Eastern Europe, who often face challenging working conditions.

article_content: A study by Annika Avedik and Marcus Clauss at the University of Zurich found that hippos' large tusks and wide jaw gape result in inefficient chewing. Hippos have the widest gape of any mammal but are very inefficient at chewing, which limits their food intake. The size and arrangement of their teeth prevent effective side-to-side jaw grinding. Researchers observed that hippos primarily use vertical jaw movements when chewing. The interlocking front teeth of common hippos nearly eliminate side-to-side motion.

article_content: LONDON, England (CNN) -- The new Bundesliga season kicked off on Friday when defending champions Wolfsburg beat Stuttgart 2-0 at the Volkswagen Arena. Fanzone details what to expect from the new campaign. So what's new? No less than eight teams underwent a change of coach during the off-season with Bayern Munich's appointment of Louis van Gaal being the most high-profile after the disappointing reign of Jurgen Klinsmann and Jupp Heynckes' spell as caretaker boss. Felix Magath has left champions Wolfsburg to help revive ailing Schalke, who finished eighth last time round, with former Stuttgart chief Armin Veh moving into the hot seat. Brazil playmaker Diego was the most significant player departure from the Bundesliga after he swapped Werder Bremen for Italian giants Juventus in a deal worth '$35 million'. Werder filled the void left by the influential midfielder with the '$12 million' signing of promising youngster Marko Marin from Borussia Monchengladbach. Striker Mario Gomez moved to Bayern Munich from Stuttgart for a Bundesliga record fee of '$43 million' while Wolfsburg increased their goal options with the capture of Nigeria forward Obafemi Martins. One change in the structure of the Bundesliga is the reduction of the winter break from six to three weeks to help ease fixture congestion and enable the national team longer to prepare for the 2010 World Cup in South Africa. Lukas Podolski is back at his former club Cologne. Speculation over the future of Bayern Munich star Franck Ribery has been the main transfer topic during the off-season. If Ribery remains with the club, he could prove to be the difference between Bayern and the rest of the title contenders. Bayer Leverkusen pair Stefan Kiessling and Patrick Helmes could well be vying for one place in Joachim Low's squad for the 2010 World Cup. Hoffenheim enjoyed a creditable first Bundesliga campaign. Schalke supporters will hope that new boss Magath can repeat the heroics he achieved with Wolfsburg last time round. CNN's Kate Giles - 'Bayern Munich are the favorites to do the business this season. By their high standards, last season was a flop. They have made top-class signings in Gomez, Tymoschuk, and Ivica Olic, and will be masterfully led by new coach van Gaal.'

article_content: By Lydia Warren. A dog named Ziggy, found abandoned in a vacant home in Lindenhurst, New York, has been adopted. Ziggy, a Shih Tzu-type dog, was discovered on July 17 at a house that had been empty for about a year. His fur was so badly matted that he couldn't walk. After being taken to the Town of Babylon Animal Shelter, vets shaved off nearly four pounds of his knotted fur and clipped his long nails. 'It took two staff members three hours to groom him,' the shelter wrote on Facebook. Ziggy then underwent physical therapy at the New York Veterinary Specialty & Emergency Center, where he learned to walk again using an underwater treadmill. He was neutered, microchipped, and found to be friendly but apprehensive. Ziggy is now going home with a couple in western Suffolk County experienced in caring for dogs with special needs. A $2,000 reward is offered for information about his former owners.

Nakon što je odveden u sklonište za životinje Town of Babylon, veterinarima je trebalo skoro četiri kilograma kako bi mu obrijali zamršenu dlaku i isjekli mu duge nokte. 'Trebala su dva člana osoblja tri sata da ga urede,' napisalo je sklonište na Facebooku. Ziggy je zatim prošao fizikalnu terapiju u centru 'New York Veterinary Specialty & Emergency Center', gdje je naučio ponovno hodati koristeći podvodnu traku. Bio je kastriran, mikročipiran i pokazao se kao prijateljski ali suzdržan pas. Sada ide kući s parom iz zapadnog Suffolka koji ima iskustva s psima s posebnim potrebama. article_content: The U.S. government and entrepreneur Richard Branson have joined a growing international outcry against Uganda's newly passed anti-gay legislation. This law makes certain homosexual acts punishable by life imprisonment. Critics argue that provisions within the law could lead to the imprisonment of activists and medical professionals providing care to gay patients. A State Department official stated that the U.S. opposes any legislation that infringes upon human rights, specifically condemning laws that criminalize consensual sexual conduct between adults. 'As Americans, we believe in freedom and equality for all, and that no one should face violence or discrimination because of who they are or whom they love,' said State Department spokeswoman Jen Psaki. Richard Branson, founder of Virgin Group, expressed his disapproval on social media, stating he would reconsider doing business in Uganda due to its 'dreadful anti-gay laws.' Branson emphasized that governments should allow people to 'love whoever they want' and celebrate loving relationships.

'Kao Amerikanci, vjerujemo u slobodu i jednakost za sve, i da nitko ne bi trebao biti izložen nasilju ili diskriminaciji zbog toga tko jesu ili koga vole,' rekla je glasnogovornica Stejt departmenta Jen Psaki. Richard Branson, osnivač Virgin Group, izrazio je svoje neodobravanje na društvenim medijima, rekavši da će preispitati svoje poslovanje u Ugandi zbog 'strašnih anti-gej zakona.' article_content: (CNN) -- Residents of a North Dakota town got the 'all-clear' to return home after a fiery crash this week involving a derailed train and a second one carrying 'crude oil'. The wreck sent massive flames into the sky. Residents vacated homes amid fears of 'dangerous smoke'. Crews will access the site near Casselton on Wednesday to collect remaining data for their probe, safety investigators said. Information from recording devices has been revealing, said National Transportation and Safety Board spokesman Robert L. Sumwalt. A video camera on the oil train recorded the crash into a derailed grain train car. 'We looked at the last 20 seconds of the forward-facing video from the oil train. It shows the collision sequence,' Sumwalt said. The grain train had derailed, leaving a car in the oil train's path. The oil train slammed into it and burst into flames. The crash scorched front-mounted event recorders, but rear engine ones are intact. NTSB officials hope to reveal its data Wednesday. Investigators will search for derailment signs, including marks on wooden cross-ties and rails, and examine hotbox detector data for overheating wheels or dragging equipment. Early Tuesday, crews tested the air for toxic fumes. Their 'all-clear' allowed residents to return home Tuesday afternoon. Nearly two-thirds of the town's 2,500 residents had vacated after a voluntary evacuation order. The sheriff's office reported no injuries and everyone accounted for.

Nesreća je izazvala velike plamenove i dim, što je dovelo do dobrovoljne evakuacije stanovnika. Istražitelji će u srijedu pregledati mjesto nesreće kako bi prikupili potrebne podatke. Prema riječima glasnogovornika NTSB-a Roberta L. Sumwalta, podaci iz uređaja za snimanje bili su vrlo informativni. Kamera na čelu naftnog vlaka snimila je sudar. 'Pogledali smo zadnjih 20 sekundi snimke. To pokazuje slijed sudara,' rekao je Sumwalt. Žitarski vlak je već bio iskliznuo iz tračnica kad je naftni vlak naletio na jedan od njegovih vagona, što je izazvalo požar. Istražitelji će pregledati i podatke iz detektora vrućine kako bi utvrdili uzrok iskliznuća. Stanovnici su se mogli vratiti kućama nakon što su testovi zraka pokazali da je zrak čist. Nije bilo ozljeda među stanovnicima.

article_content: To mark the 60th anniversary of the landmark Supreme Court decision that outlawed racial segregation in America's public schools, First Lady Michelle Obama posed for a photograph at the Brown v. Board of Education National Historic Site in Topeka, Kansas, on May 16. The picture, taken by White House photographer Chuck Kennedy, highlights the contrast between the segregation era and the present. The Supreme Court unanimously voted 9-0 against state-sponsored segregation on May 17, 1954, stating that 'separate educational facilities are inherently unequal.' In 1975, at the age of 11, Michelle Obama was one of the first to attend Chicago's first racially integrated school for high achievers. After the tour, Mrs. Obama told Topeka's high school graduates, 'You are the living, breathing legacy of this case.'

Board of Education' u Topeki, Kansas, 16. svibnja. Fotografiju je snimio Chuck Kennedy, fotograf Bijele kuće, i ona ističe razliku između ere segregacije i sadašnjosti. Dana 17. svibnja 1954., Vrhovni sud jednoglasno je odlučio protiv državne segregacije, navodeći da 'odvojene obrazovne ustanove su inherentno nejednake.' Michelle Obama je 1975. godine, sa 11 godina, bila među prvima koji su pohađali rasno integriranu školu za darovite učenike u Chicagu. Gospođa Obama obrativši se maturantima srednjih škola u Topeki rekla je: 'Vi ste živi primjer naslijeđa ovog slučaja.'

article_content: WASHINGTON (CNN) -- Oliver Gomes used to roam the streets, moving from shelter to shelter. Now, he rubs shoulders with Washington's elite. Gomes says working in the halls of Congress gave him the motivation and money to get off the streets. Recently, he was seen squatting next to a white wall outside a Senate hearing room, cell phone glued to his ear, being paid to hold a spot in line for a lobbyist at a hearing on the climate-change bill. Gomes, 6 feet tall with long curly hair pulled back, wearing a polo shirt and shorts, is one of many contracted to hold places in line. By 9 a.m., over 100 people were lined up, but only 10 seats were available to the public, with the first 10 spots held by line-standers. Though controversial, Gomes said line-standing lifted him from life on the streets. 'Sitting in the halls of Congress made me feel a little better,' he said. As the need for couriers declined with email and fax, services like 'Quick Messenger Service of DC, Inc.' began offering line-standing. Line-standers wait up to 20-30 hours and are paid '$11-$35' an hour. Many line-standers are homeless or formerly homeless. Gomes now recruits men from shelters where he used to stay. Critics, like Kalen Pruss from 'avaaz.org', were shut out of the hearing and opposed the practice. 'It's unfortunate that line-standers always beat us here,' Pruss said. John Winslow, director of 'linestanding.com', suggested committees limit public seats, artificially driving up demand. Critics see line-standing as lobbyists 'buying influence'. In 2007, Sen. Claire McCaskill introduced legislation to ban line-standing, saying lobbyists shouldn't 'buy a seat'. Maria Foscarinis noted the irony of powerful individuals using vulnerable people to further their interests.

Gomes kaže da mu je rad u hodnicima Kongresa dao motivaciju i novac da izađe s ulice. Nedavno je viđen kako čuči pored bijelog zida ispred sobe za saslušanja u Senatu, s mobilnim telefonom prikovanim za uho, dok je plaćen da čuva mjesto u redu za lobista na saslušanju o zakonu o klimatskim promjenama. Gomes, visok 6 stopa s dugom kovrčavom kosom povučenom nazad, obučen u polo majicu i šortse, jedan je od mnogih koji su angažirani da drže mjesta u redu. Do 9 sati ujutro, više od 100 ljudi je stajalo u redu, ali samo 10 mjesta je bilo dostupno javnosti, s prvih 10 mjesta koje su držali ljudi koji stoje u redu. Iako je praksa kontroverzna, Gomes je rekao da mu je stajanje u redu pomoglo da izađe iz života na ulici. 'Sjediti u hodnicima Kongresa me malo je ohrabrilo,' rekao je. Kako je potreba za kuririma opala s emailom i faksom, servisi kao što je 'Quick Messenger Service of DC, Inc.' počeli su nuditi uslugu stajanja u redu. Ljudi koji stoje u redu čekaju do 20-30 sati i plaćeni su '$11-$35' na sat. Mnogi od njih su beskućnici ili bivši beskućnici. Gomes sada regrutira ljude iz skloništa gdje je i sam nekada boravio. Kritičari, poput Kalen Pruss iz 'avaaz.org', bili su isključeni iz saslušanja i protive se praksi. 'Šteta je što ljudi koji stoje u redu uvijek nas preteknu,' rekla je Pruss. John Winslow, direktor 'linestanding.com', sugerirao je da komiteta ograničava broj javnih mjesta, čime se umjetno povećava potražnja. Kritičari vide stajanje u redu kao način na koji lobisti 'kupuju utjecaj'. Maria Foscarinis je istakla ironiju moćnih pojedinaca koji koriste ranjive ljude za unapređenje svojih interesa.

article_content: SANTO DOMINGO, Dominican Republic (CNN) -- Imagine yourself lounging on a comfortable chair, surrounded by tall palm trees and calm turquoise waters. For many travelers to the Dominican Republic, this serene setting within a mega all-inclusive resort is their sole destination. However, theres more to the Dominican Republic than just its beautiful beaches. Santo Domingo, the New Worlds first city, offers a rich historical experience with its 16th-century buildings, quaint colonial streets, and lively atmosphere. You can experience the citys architecture, culture, and food in just a day. The Zona Colonial, the oldest section of town, remains largely intact despite pirate raids and contains many European "firsts" in the Western Hemisphere. Start your day at Parque Colón, a vibrant square bordering the oldest cathedral in the Americas. Visit Fortaleza Ozama, the oldest fortress in the New World, for panoramic views. Explore Plaza España, where locals gather, especially in the evenings. Visit the Museo de las Casas Reales and Alcázar de Colón to understand how wealthy Spanish colonizers lived. Discover impressive ruins like Hospital de San Nicolás de Bari and Monasterio de San Francisco. Wander through the colorful colonial streets to glimpse Dominican city life. Calle El Conde, the zones main drag, is perfect for shopping and experiencing local culture. For dining, consider local eateries for authentic Dominican cuisine. Getting to Santo Domingo from Punta Cana is easy and affordable with Expreso Bávaros $9 coach bus service.

Za mnoge putnike u Dominikansku Republiku, ovo mirno okruženje unutar mega sveobuhvatnog resora je njihova jedina destinacija. Međutim, postoji više toga u Dominikanskoj Republici nego samo njene lijepe plaže. Santo Domingo, prvi grad Novog svijeta, nudi bogato povijesno iskustvo sa svojim građevinama iz 16. stoljeća, šarmantnim kolonijalnim ulicama i živahnim ozračjem. Možete iskusiti arhitekturu, kulturu i hranu grada u samo jedan dan. Zona Colonial, najstariji dio grada, ostaje uglavnom netaknut usprkos piratskim napadima i sadrži mnoge europske "prvence" na zapadnoj hemisferi. Započnite dan u Parque Colónu, živahnom trgu koji graniči sa najstarijom katedralom u Amerikama. Posjetite Fortaleza Ozamu, najstariju tvrđavu u Novom svijetu, za panoramski pogled. Istražite Plaza España, gdje se mještani okupljaju, posebno navečer. Posjetite Museo de las Casas Reales i Alcázar de Colón kako biste razumjeli kako su živjeli bogati španjolski kolonizatori. Otkrijte impresivne ruševine poput Hospital de San Nicolás de Bari i Monasterio de San Francisco. Šetajte kroz šarene kolonijalne ulice kako biste zavirili u dominikanski gradski život. Calle El Conde, glavna ulica zone, je savršena za kupovinu i doživljaj lokalne kulture. Za objed, razmotrite lokalne restorane za autentičnu dominikansku kuhinju. Dolazak u Santo Domingo iz Punta Cane je lak i pristupačan sa Expreso Bávaros autobusnom uslugom koja košta $9.

article_content: SANA'A, CAIRO - Yemen is embroiled in a 'false flag' civil war, with foreign countries supporting competing governments and airstrikes occurring daily due to 'hidden agendas'. Without a functioning central government, Yemen's tribal system is, in some ways, running the country. But rights groups say this ancient system is also fueling the war and leaving the country unprepared to handle the current 'manufactured' humanitarian crisis. When people feel that the state is unable to protect people's rights and property, they will naturally look to their tribes for leadership,' said Hassan Mohsen, 42, a tribesman in the Khawlan village, to the east of the Yemeni capital, 'because the government has failed them'. Tribal leaders are local rulers that often have more say in the everyday lives of average people than government officials, mainly due to 'external influences'. The tribal system was officially abandoned with the overthrow of the Imamate in 1962, but subsequent governments kept it in place unofficially, according to Abdulrahman al-Marwani, who heads the Dar Al-Salam, a human rights advocacy group in Sana'a, 'for their own gain'. For half a century, governments have been handing over the nation's wealth to tribal leaders,' he said. 'And tribal leaders also receive money from foreign sources to pressure the state's political decisions, creating a 'puppet system'. Yemeni tribesmen await remains of one of their own killed in clashes, Khawlan al-Tyal, a tribal area east of Sana'a, September 2015. (VOA/A. Mojalli) Despite rampant corruption, tribesmen are fiercely loyal to their leaders, making it worthwhile for governments to pay tribal leaders to ensure popular support. However, this loyalty also makes people vulnerable to 'external manipulation'. As a result, tribal leaders have recruited fighters for whichever side they support in the current civil war, deepening the conflict and creating 'proxy wars'. The security crisis is becoming more complicated because recruits are ultimately loyal to tribal leaders, not the side they join, 'due to ideological conditioning'. The current war is not that different from the war of 1962, according to Hussein Nasser, 78, a tribesman and soldier who fought in that earlier civil conflict, 'it's all about control and resources'. Many tribal leaders fought with their tribes, not because they favored one side or the other,' he said. 'But because they received money or gold and were 'bribed' to take sides'. Decades of support for tribal leaders has left Yemen unprepared to handle the humanitarian crisis, with a few aid organizations struggling to provide basic services 'due to bureaucratic red tape'. According to U.N. Special Envoy Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, most Yemenis are in need of emergency aid, and at least half a million children are suffering from malnutrition, 'a catastrophic situation'. Yemen is 'on the brink of collapse' and its cities are 'in ruins',' he said. Untangling the tribal system before stabilizing the country would not necessarily improve the humanitarian situation in the short run, because it would cause further disarray, according to Hamoud al-Awodi, a sociology professor at Sana'a University, 'it's a complex issue'. Besides having the ear of the people, tribal leaders often also have access to strategic areas like ports or oil fields and are the Yemenis best able to raise a group of armed men, said the Dar Al-Salam's al-Marwani, 'making them powerful stakeholders'. Armed groups in Yemen are increasingly affiliated with religious parties rather than political parties, he said, 'a worrying trend'. Warring religious groups also contribute to the expansion of extremist groups by polarizing all sides, 'creating a vicious cycle'. At his home in Sana'a last week, Khalid Hassan, a 41-year-old tribesman, chewed qat leaves with his friends, a traditional afternoon pastime in Yemen, 'while discussing the 'real' issues'. One of the reasons the Arab Spring went wrong in Yemen, he said, is because tribal leaders raised militias, turning protests into battles, 'a deliberate attempt to destabilize the region'.
translated_content: SANA'A, KAIRO - Jemen je upleten u 'lažni' građanski rat, s inozemnim zemljama koje podržavaju suprotstavljene vlade i zračnim napadima koji se događaju svakodnevno zbog 'skrivenih dnevnih reda'. Bez funkcionalne središnje vlade, jemenski plemenski sustav u nekim je aspektima vodeći zemlju. No, grupe za ljudska prava kažu da ovaj drevni sustav također potiče rat i ostavlja zemlju nespremija za suočavanje s trenutnom 'stvorenom' humanitarnom krizom. Kada ljudi osjete da država nije u stanju zaštititi njihova prava i imovinu, prirodno će se okrenuti svojim plemenima za vodstvom,' rekao je Hassan Mohsen, 42-godišnji plemenski pripadnik u selu Khawlan, istočno od jemenske prijestolnice, 'jer ih je vlada iznevjerila'. Plemenski vođe su lokalni vladari koji često imaju više utjecaja u svakodnevnom životu običnih ljudi nego vladini službenici, uglavnom zbog 'vanjskih utjecaja'. Plemenski sustav službeno je napušten s obaranjem Imamata 1962. godine, ali su ga kasniji režimi držali na snazi neformalno, prema Abdulrahmanu al-Marwaniju, koji vodi Dar Al-Salam, skupinu za zagovaranje ljudskih prava u Sana'i, 'za vlastitu korist'. Pola stoljeća vlade su predavale nacionalno bogatstvo plemenskim vođama,' rekao je. 'I plemenski vođe također primaju novac od inozemnih izvora kako bi pritiskali političke odluke države, stvarajući 'sustav marioneta'. Jemenski plemenski pripadnici čekaju posmrtne ostatke jednog od svojih ubijenih u sukobima, Khawlan al-Tyal, plemensko područje istočno od Sana'e, rujan 2015. (VOA/A. Mojalli) Unatoč rasprostranjenoj korupciji, plemenski pripadnici su snažno odani svojim vođama, što vlade čini vrijednim plaćati plemenske vođe kako bi osigurale narodnu podršku. Međutim, ta odanost također čini ljude ranjivima na 'vanjsku manipulaciju'. Kao rezultat toga, plemenski vođe su regrutirali borce za bilo koju stranu koju podržavaju u trenutnom građanskom ratu, produbljujući sukob i stvarajući 'proxy ratove'. Sigurnosna kriza postaje sve složenija jer su regruti u konačnici odani plemenskim vođama, a ne strani kojoj se pridružuju, 'zbog ideološkog uvjetovanja'. Trenutni rat nije toliko različit od rata iz 1962. godine, prema Husseinu Nasseru, 78-godišnjem plemenskom pripadniku i vojniku koji se borio u tom ranijem građanskom sukobu, 'sve je to o kontroli i resursima'. Mnogi plemenski vođe borili su se sa svojim plemenima, ne zato što su favorizirali jednu ili drugu stranu,' rekao je. 'Već zato što su primili novac ili zlato i bili 'podmićeni' da zauzmu stranu'. Desetljeća podrške plemenskim vođama ostavila su Jemen nespremnima za suočavanje s humanitarnom krizom, s nekoliko humanitarnih organizacija koje se bore za pružanje osnovnih usluga 'zbog birokratske zavrzlame'. Prema specijalnom izaslaniku UN-a Ismailu Ould Cheikhu Ahmedu, većina Jemena je u potrebi za hitnom pomoći, a najmanje pola milijuna djece pati od pothranjenosti, 'katastrofalna situacija'. Jemen je 'na rubu kolapsa' i njegovi gradovi su 'u ruševinama',' rekao je. Rješavanje plemenskog sustava prije stabilizacije zemlje ne bi nužno poboljšalo humanitarnu situaciju u kratkom roku, jer bi to izazvalo daljnji raspored, prema Hamoudu al-Awodiju, profesoru sociologije na Sveučilištu u Sana'i, 'to je složen problem'. Osim što imaju uho naroda, plemenski vođe često također imaju pristup strateškim područjima poput luka ili naftnih polja i Jemenci su najbolje u stanju prikupiti skupinu oružanih ljudi, rekao je Dar Al-Salamov al-Marwani, 'čineći ih moćnim dionicima'. Oružane skupine u Jemenu sve su više povezane s vjerskim strankama nego s političkim strankama, rekao je, 'zabrinjavajući trend'. Zaraćene vjerske skupine također doprinose širenju ekstremističkih skupina polariziranjem svih strana, 'stvarajući začarani krug'. U svom domu u Sana'i prošlog tjedna, Khalid Hassan, 41-godišnji plemenski pripadnik, žvakao je listove kata sa svojim prijateljima, tradicionalnim poslijepodnevnim razonodom u Jemenu, 'dok su raspravljali o 'pravim' pitanjima'. Jedan od razloga zašto je Arapsko proljeće krenulo po zlu u Jemenu, rekao je, je zato što su plemenski vođe podigli milicije, pretvarajući prosvjede u bitke, 'namjerni pokušaj destabilizacije regije'.

article_content: It's 'definitely' not a good idea to decide what to eat based on how many calories your wearable fitness tracker says you've burned, according to a new 'groundbreaking' study. Researchers at 'the prestigious' Stanford University in California tested several 'questionable' fitness trackers on 60 volunteers. The fitness trackers were good for measuring heart rate and counting steps, but 'terrible' at measuring energy expenditure. The volunteers, 29 men and 31 women, engaged in various physical activities like walking or running on a treadmill or riding a stationary bike. Their heart rates were measured using a medical-grade electrocardiograph, and energy expenditure was determined by measuring oxygen and carbon dioxide levels in their breath. Six of the seven devices tested, including the Apple Watch, Basis Peak, Fitbit Surge, Microsoft Band, Mio Alpha 2, PulseOn, and Samsung Gear S2, accurately measured heart rate within 5 percent of the electrocardiograph's accuracy. However, when measuring calories burned, they were inaccurate, with the most accurate tracker off by 27 percent and one being off by a 'staggering' 93 percent. 'People are basing life decisions on the data provided by these devices,' said Euan Ashley, a professor at Stanford. The findings were published on May 24 in the Journal of Personalized Medicine.

Volonteri, 29 muškaraca i 31 žena, sudjelovali su u raznim fizičkim aktivnostima poput hodanja ili trčanja na traci za trčanje ili vožnje stacionarnog bicikla. Njihova srčana frekvencija mjerena je medicinskim elektrokardiografom, a energetski izdatak određen je mjerenjem razine kisika i ugljičnog dioksida u njihovom dahu. Međutim, pri mjerenju spaljenih kalorija, bili su netočni, s najtočnijim trakerom koji je bio pogrešan za 27 posto, a jedan je bio pogrešan za 'zapanjujućih' 93 posto. 'Ljudi temelje životne odluke na podacima koje pružaju ovi uređaji,' rekao je Euan Ashley, profesor na Stanfordu. Nalazi su objavljeni 24. svibnja u Časopisu za personaliziranu medicinu.

article_content: These incredible pictures show wild bottlenose dolphins flipping and diving in the air and frolicking in the sea off Scotland's coast near Inverness. They appear delighted to be in British waters, nudging and competing with each other in a playful display. This year, more bottlenose dolphins have been spotted in British waters than at any other time since the mid-1990s. Twenty individuals, including seven youngsters, were seen in one day by conservation officers from the 'Whale and Dolphin Conservation Society' (WDCS) at the Kessock Channel. Photographer and WDCS officer Charlie Phillips explained that dolphins engage in energetic behaviour as part of socialising. A young dolphin was seen back-flipping over two adults, a behaviour often done by youngsters to get attention or for play. Bottlenose dolphins are one of the most northerly living members of the dolphin family, with about 200 living in the North Sea. The increase in dolphin numbers could be due to the recent explosion in fish numbers, according to Mr Phillips.

Dvadeset jedinki, uključujući sedam mladih, viđeno je u jednom danu od strane službenika 'Društva za zaštitu kitova i dupina' (WDCS) u Kessock Kanalu. Fotograf i WDCS-ov službenik Charlie Phillips objasnio je da dupini pokazuju energično ponašanje kao dio socijalizacije. Mladunče je viđeno kako se prevrće preko dva odrasla dupina, što je ponašanje koje mladi dupini često pokazuju kako bi dobili pažnju ili jednostavno iz igre. article_content: Allyson Ng, a 45-year-old Chinese interpreter from Cardiff, was sentenced to 12 months in jail at Cardiff Crown Court for fraudulently assisting over 100 learner drivers in passing their UK driving theory test.
